question: Do the simplex cutout fixes outside N06.4's domain, router.java_quirks.cutout_hole_crosses_border=false (the stand-in division line of a corner on the outer border no longer clips later pieces, so no piece of a hole crossing the border vanishes) and router.java_quirks.simplex_octagon_half_corner=false (a corner that is not an integer point and lies on no outer border line is divided at its exact point, so the pieces beside it no longer overlap), each alone and both, keep the unrouted total within N02's totals rule (accept no-regress: correctness fixes) of Java's cutouts, with no via in a pad, no copper below the minimum and no new clearance or DRC error; do the 45 degree rows keep Java's sessions byte for byte; and how often does a run reach the two switches? pairs_rule: the verdict pair (baseline, all) is judged by the totals block with the hard and guard metrics below; the reported pairs (baseline, cutout_hole_crosses_border) and (baseline, simplex_octagon_half_corner) are the switch-by-switch bisection (N06's decisions: one switch per bug), run up front. boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number. Chosen before any routed number: the switches reach a drill page only in any-angle mode, so A07's three any-angle variants (the boards N06.12 registered for any-angle mode) are the measured rows; two 45 degree boards of n06-g.txt check that nothing changes where the switches are not reached; canary-pwr also goes through the KiCad plugin path (plugin_canary); amendment 1 adds fixtures/Issue756-tomu-fpga8.dsn and Issue756-tomu-fpga9.dsn, the only corpus boards where the newly wired splits reach a switch (branch 3: 1 and 6 cutouts of their stored areas, corpus_counter_note), chosen before any route under this registration; both are 45 degree boards, identity checks for N06.14's own arms

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: amendment 1, no new breach versus baseline (N06.4's amendment 2): an arm's via_in_pad is its count of vias in an SMD pad that the input has no via with that centre, padstack and nets for (main 4885a30's added_via_in_pad, on the imported SES; plugin canary: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py) minus the baseline arm's count on the same row, floored at 0; the raw count is reported as via_in_pad_raw
metric_definitions.below_minimum: amendment 1, no new breach versus baseline (N06.4's amendment 2): on a DSN row, the number of the arm's delivered traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input board does not already have, minus the baseline arm's number on the same row, floored at 0 (the router's pin neck-down puts copper under every class width by design, so the baseline breaks the raw count); the raw count is reported as below_minimum_raw and the nets under their class width (freerouting-dev widths, under_mm > 0) as below_class_width_nets, neither judged; plugin canary: KiCad's track_width errors minus the baseline arm's, floored at 0
metric_definitions.clearance_violations: the router's clearance violations of the final board (RESULT board_statistics; gate collect's clearance_violations)
metric_definitions.drc_real: plugin canary only: KiCad error-severity items other than unconnected items
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: plugin canary only: KiCad's unconnected items after the import (canary grade.sh); the totals signal where it is a number
metric_definitions.unrouted: gate collect's unrouted (connections.incomplete_count) of the final board; the totals signal of the DSN rows, which have no KiCad board
metric_definitions.session_differences: n06_run.py: 1 when the arm's SES differs from the baseline's
metric_definitions.cutout_hole_crosses_border_reached: STATS total.counts.cutout_hole_crosses_border_reached: the simplex cutout pieces whose first-division-line clip differs between the two arms of the switch, counted in both arms
metric_definitions.simplex_octagon_half_corner_reached: STATS total.counts.simplex_octagon_half_corner_reached: the simplex cutout corners that are not integer points and lie on no outer border line, counted in both arms
metric_definitions.octagon_box_cutout_branch3_reached: STATS total.counts.octagon_box_cutout_branch3_reached (N06.4's counter): the drill-page and tie-pin cutouts whose branch 3 changes a piece, counted in both arms. The newly wired splits are not counted per run; corpus_counter_command counts them per board

paired_rule_note: pass_rule is retained for gate parser validation; the registered verdict uses totals with accept=no-regress
keep_rule: N06's accept rule for (b) fixes: a batch is accepted when the hard guards hold, no board regresses by more than twice its noise band and the total is not worse than the set's noise; a neutral fix stays in. If the verdict pair passes, N06.13 turns both switches off in ENHANCED through N05. Amendment 1, the pair (baseline, octagon_box_cutout_branch3): pass keeps N06.4's acceptance at the wider reach (N06.13 may promote the switch); fail is an operator decision: promote the switch without the wider reach (a separate switch for the newly wired splits), or not at all
accept: Unit and invariant tests pin both behaviours of both switches (tests/cutout_invariant.rs: java_breaks_the_invariant_outside_the_two_rows, all_fixed_cutouts_tile_the_rest_on_the_extended_set, java_breaks_the_extended_set_through_each_switch).
On the two 45 degree rows every arm's sessions equal the baseline's and both reach counters are 0.
The verdict pair passes the totals rule (no-regress) with the hard and guard metrics.
Grade canary-pwr through the KiCad plugin path; no new real DRC, via-in-pad or below-minimum errors.

Amendment 1: the pair (baseline, octagon_box_cutout_branch3) passes the same totals rule (no-regress) with the hard and guard metrics, so N06.4's acceptance of octagon_box_cutout_branch3 holds at the wider reach.
